dedupe_keys.name: machine learning models for the evaluation of the lateral spreading hazard in the avon river area following the 2011 christchurch earthquake

description: Machine Learning Models for the Evaluation of the Lateral Spreading Hazard in the Avon River Area Following the 2011 Christchurch Earthquake is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Maria Giovanna Durante, University of Calabria (unical.it). This project contains a Jupyter Notebook and python codes to run a suite of machine learning Random Forest Classifier algorithms to predict liquefaction induced lateral spreading displacement. This study is trained using data from the 2011 Christchurch earthquake in the Avon River area. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-3zdj-4937. Keywords: machine learning; random forest; liquefaction; lateral spreading; 2011 Christchurch earthquake.. Published 2021-03-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is GPL-3.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
